The method operates on the standard 3DGS Gaussian representation [S1, unofficial]:

The claim states that the method operates on the standard 3DGS Gaussian representation. The provided evidence (Source [S1]) explicitly reviews the standard 3DGS representation in Section 3.1, defining the scene as a set of 3D Gaussians with specific parameters (position, opacity, rotation, base-scale, covariance, and spherical-harmonic coefficients). It further details the standard rendering equations (projected covariance, alpha compositing, and alpha value calculation) and the standard objective function. The subsequent sections describe how the proposed method (EffGS) builds upon this standard representation by adding frequency-aware guidance, localized density control, and adaptive primitive scale modulation, rather than replacing the fundamental representation itself. Therefore, the evidence supports the claim that the method operates on the standard 3DGS Gaussian representation.
